name: Sayuri
source:
A pet parrot who was owned by the [url=https://vndb.org/c14295]caretaker of the Gourd Lake boat rental shop[/url], and lived there alongside her owner. 

[spoiler]
Polly's owner was Yanni Yogi, who named her after his late fiancée Polly Jenkins. When Yogi was accused of murdering [url=https://vndb.org/c14120]Gregory Edgeworth[/url] in the high-profile "DL-6" case, his defense attorney, [url=https://vndb.org/c14285]Robert Hammond[/url], argued a successful insanity plea. Though Yogi escaped conviction, the case destroyed his social standing, and Jenkins committed suicide. 

Yogi taught Polly to talk, though she would only respond if her name was said first. Among the things Yogi taught Polly were the combination to his safe and to respond with "Don't forget DL-6!" when asked if someone had forgotten something. 

Polly remained in Yogi's shack as his only company after DL-6. She was therefore present when Yogi met with Hammond inside the shack fifteen years after DL-6 and murdered him. When [url=https://vndb.org/c10833]Miles Edgeworth[/url] was arrested for the murder, Miles's lawyer [url=https://vndb.org/c3941]Phoenix Wright[/url] and Wright's assistant [url=https://vndb.org/c3944]Maya Fey[/url] entered the shack during their investigation. They were shocked when Polly mentioned the safe combination and DL-6.

Yogi testified as a witness in Miles's trial, but when Wright found inconsistencies in the testimony, Yogi fled, leaving Polly in the shack. Fey was eager to adopt the bird, but Wright said that the police would likely do something about her.

Yogi was eventually captured, though he claimed that he had only gone to get food for Polly; he stated that Polly was "a bit of a gourmand" and would only eat high-quality bird pellets from France, which could only be bought from a "big pet shop downtown". He claimed that he was on his way back to his shack when he was arrested.

When Wright struggled to get information from Yogi, prosecutor [url=https://vndb.org/c14292]Manfred von Karma[/url] taunted him, stating, "Perhaps you'd like to cross-examine the parrot for a little comic relief, hmm?". Against everyone's expectations, Wright decided to do exactly that and called Polly as a witness. However, Polly did not respond when asked about DL-6; it soon became apparent that von Karma had Polly retrained to avoid mentioning the case. Wright was however able to confirm her owner, who had been hiding his identity, as Yogi by linking Polly's namesake and the combination of the safe being the date DL-6 took place. Yogi, his cover blown, then confessed to the murder of Hammond.

The fact that Wright had cross-examined a parrot was one of the reasons [url=https://vndb.org/c53623]Sasha Buckler[/url] sought him out years later in defense of an orca accused of killing Jack Shipley.
[/spoiler]
